functions.name: DecompressSmackFrame
functions.comment:
Decompresses a Smack video frame using RLE palette-based decompression.

  Algorithm:
    1. Reset frame state at Smack+0x41c to zero
    2. Compute frame index: current_frame (0x374) - start_frame (0xc)
    3. If frame index < 0, skip (frame not ready)
    4. Check keyframe flag (0x14 bit 0): if set and first frame, call ReadSmackFrame
    5. Otherwise call FUN_10005440 for normal frame processing
    6. Load frame data pointer from Smack+0x3d4
    7. Read block flags byte at (Smack+0x3e0)[frame_idx]: bits 0-7 indicate 8 data blocks
    8. For each flag bit, set corresponding block pointer at 0x3e4-0x404
    9. If bit 0 set (RLE flag): copy 0xc0 (192) dwords from palette to stack
   10. RLE loop: decompress 0x100 (256) pixels from opcode stream
       - Opcode bit 7 set: repeat N pixels from current position
       - Opcode bit 6 set: copy N pixels from backref offset
       - Otherwise: 3 literal palette indices
   11. Verify expected frame index (0x3d8) matches actual; set error if mismatch

  Parameters:
    pSmack (ECX via stack)  Pointer to Smack structure (1220 bytes)

  Returns:
    void - modifies Smack structure in-place:
      - Success: Smack+0x68 = 0, block pointers populated
      - Error: Smack+0x68 = 1, Smack+0x3c4 = 1

  Special Cases:
    - Frame not ready (negative index): returns immediately
    - Keyframe detection: routes to ReadSmackFrame for special handling
    - RLE decompression uses 768-byte stack buffer (192 dwords)

  Structure Layout (Smack offsets accessed):
    Offset | Size | Description
    0x0c   | 4    | Start frame index
    0x14   | 4    | Flags (bit 0 = keyframe processing)
    0x68   | 4    | Error state (0 = OK, 1 = error)
    0x6c   | 768  | Palette data (192 RGB triplets)
    0x374  | 4    | Current frame index
    0x37c  | 4    | Frame data size
    0x3c4  | 4    | Secondary error flag
    0x3d4  | 4    | Frame data pointer
    0x3d8  | 4    | Expected frame index
    0x3e0  | ptr  | Block flags array pointer
    0x3e4  | 32   | Block pointers array (8 pointers)
    0x404  | 4    | End of frame data pointer
    0x41c  | 4    | Decompression state

  Global Data:
    g_aSmackPalette (0x100142e0)  256-byte palette index lookup table

functions.name: ReadBufferedSmackFrame
functions.comment:
Reads and buffers the next Smack video frame from file with page-aligned I/O.

Algorithm:
  1. On first frame (offset 0x374 == 0), zero-initialize 0xC1 (193) DWORDs at offset 0x6C
  2. If frame slot at current index (offset 0x444) is valid (!= -1) and has data at +0x2C:
     a. Count non-empty frame slots from current index to slot 6
     b. If count matches g_dwProgressCallbackCount, reset all 7 frame streams via callback
  3. Sum all queued frame sizes from offset 0x3DC array up to frame count (offset 0x374)
  4. Check early exit flag (bit 0x200 at offset 0x390); if set, store offset and return 0
  5. Calculate target file offset: accumulated_sizes + base_offset (offset 0x3CC)
  6. Buffer management:
     a. If target within current buffer (0x468 <= target < 0x468+0x460): adjust pointers
     b. If outside buffer: call SetFilePointer, then ReadFileWithBuffer for unaligned reads
  7. Handle circular buffer wrap when current pointer exceeds end (offset 0x454)
  8. Call ReadSmackFrame to process the frame data

Parameters:
  pSmackBuffer (Stack[0x4]) -- Pointer to Smack structure containing file handle, frame queue,
    and buffer management state

Returns:
  0: Early exit when bit 0x200 is set in flags
  uint: Result from ReadSmackFrame indicating frame processing status

Special Cases:
  - Page alignment: Uses 0x1000 (4KB) pages, handles unaligned offsets with (offset & 0xFFF)
  - Circular buffer: Wraps pointer when it exceeds buffer end at offset 0x454
  - Frame callback: Resets streams via g_pfnResetSmackStream when frame count matches threshold

Structure Layout (SmackBuffer/Smack offsets used):
  Offset  Size  Field               Description
  0x006C  0x304 aFrameWorkBuffer    Working buffer area (0xC1 DWORDs initialized to 0)
  0x0374  4     dwFrameIndex        Current frame index/count
  0x0390  4     dwFlags             Status flags (bit 0x200 = skip processing)
  0x03B0  4     hFile               File handle for SetFilePointer
  0x03CC  4     dwBaseFileOffset    Base file offset for frame data
  0x03D0  4     dwCumulativeOffset  Accumulated offset for frame positioning  
  0x03D4  4     dwUpdatedOffset     Updated offset after early exit
  0x03DC  4     pFrameSizes         Pointer to array of frame sizes
  0x0428  28    aFrameSlots[7]      Array of 7 frame slot pointers
  0x0444  4     nCurrentSlotIndex   Current frame slot index (0-6 or -1)
  0x0450  4     pBufferStart        Start of file I/O buffer
  0x0454  4     pBufferEnd          End boundary for circular wrap
  0x0458  4     pBufferCurrent      Current read position in buffer
  0x045C  4     pBufferLimit        Upper limit pointer
  0x0460  4     dwBufferRemaining   Bytes remaining in buffer
  0x0464  4     dwBufferSize        Total buffer capacity
  0x0468  4     dwCurrentFileOffset Current file position

functions.name: FindFirstSetBitAndClear
functions.comment:
Finds the first set bit in a bitmask and clears it.

Algorithm:
  1. Initialize bit index to 0, bit mask to 0x2000 (bit 13)
  2. Loop through up to 7 bits:
     a. Test if current bit mask matches any bits in *pMask
     b. If match found: clear the bit from *pMask and return bit index
     c. Increment bit index, shift bit mask left (multiply by 2)
  3. If no bits found after 7 iterations, return 0xff (not found)

Parameters:
  pMask - pointer to 32-bit bitmask value; bits are tested from 0x2000
          (bit 13) through 0x4000000 (bit 26). Matched bit is cleared.

Returns:
  0-6: bit index of first set bit found (0x2000 through 0x4000000)
  0xff: no bits found in range

functions.name: InitializeSmackAudioBuffer
functions.comment:
Initializes the audio playback buffer for a specified Smack audio track.

Algorithm:
  1. Ensure Windows sound system is initialized via SmackSoundUseWin if callback not set
  2. Extract track information from pSmack->abHeader[0x48 + track*4]
  3. Check if track is enabled (bit 0x40000000) and extract sample rate (bits 0-23)
  4. Return early if sample rate is 0
  5. Extract audio format flags from byte at bits 24-31:
     - Bit 5: Stereo flag (1 = stereo, 0 = mono)
     - Bit 4: 16-bit flag (1 = 16-bit, 0 = 8-bit)
  6. Calculate frame size = (stereo+1) * (16bit+1) * sample_rate
  7. Allocate global audio buffer (0x2000 bytes) if not already allocated
  8. Get audio context pointer from pSmack->abPadding[-0x5c + track*4]
  9. Zero-initialize audio context structure (0x25 dwords = 0x94 bytes)
  10. Calculate buffer sizes:
      - Offset 0x1c: (framesize * 0x400 * microsPerFrame) / 100000
      - Offset 0x28: framesize * 0x200
      - Offset 0x18: ((size_0x1c >> 9) + framesize + 0xfff) & 0xfffff000, minimum 0x2000
  11. Allocate audio buffer of calculated size
  12. Set up buffer pointers:
      - Offset 0x08: buffer start
      - Offset 0x0c: buffer start (duplicate)
      - Offset 0x00: size from offset 0x0c
      - Offset 0x04: end = start + size
  13. Store audio format parameters:
      - Offset 0x14 (5): frame size
      - Offset 0x48: sample rate
      - Offset 0x50: stereo flag
      - Offset 0x54: 16-bit flag
  14. Call sound callback with audio context and microseconds per frame
  15. If callback fails, free allocated buffer and return error
  16. Store compressed audio data offset at context+0x38
  17. Mark this track as first audio track if none set (pSmack->abHeader[0x444] == -1)
  18. Increment global progress counter and return success

Parameters:
  pSmack         Smack* - Pointer to Smack video context structure (ECX/Stack[0x4])
  byAudioTrack   byte - Audio track index, 0-6 (Stack[0x8])

Returns:
  Success: 0x00000001 with incremented counter in upper bytes
  Failure: 0 if global buffer allocation fails
           0 if track buffer allocation fails
           Error code if sound callback fails

Special Cases:
  - Returns early with masked track info if sample rate is 0
  - Initializes Windows sound system on first call
  - Reuses global audio buffer across all tracks (0x2000 bytes)
  - Minimum track buffer size enforced at 0x2000 bytes
  - First enabled audio track is recorded in pSmack->abHeader[0x444]

Smack Audio Context Structure (pSmack->abPadding[-0x5c + track*4]):
  Offset  Size  Field           Type    Description
  0x00    4     dwBufferSize    DWORD   Size of audio buffer
  0x04    4     dwBufferEnd     DWORD   End pointer (start + size)
  0x08    4     pBufferStart    void*   Audio buffer start pointer
  0x0c    4     pBufferCopy     void*   Copy of buffer start pointer
  0x14    4     nFrameSize      int     Audio frame size in bytes
  0x18    4     dwAllocSize     DWORD   Allocated buffer size (page-aligned)
  0x1c    4     dwCalcSize1     DWORD   Calculated size parameter 1
  0x28    4     dwCalcSize2     DWORD   Calculated size parameter 2
  0x38    4     dwDataOffset    DWORD   Offset to compressed audio data
  0x48    4     dwSampleRate    DWORD   Sample rate (Hz)
  0x50    4     dwStereo        DWORD   Stereo flag (0=mono, 1=stereo)
  0x54    4     dw16Bit         DWORD   Bit depth flag (0=8bit, 1=16bit)

functions.name: SetErrorHandlingDisabled
functions.comment:
Sets the error handling disabled flag.

Algorithm:
1. Store dwDisable value to g_fErrorHandlingDisabled global

When enabled (dwDisable != 0), DisplayCriticalError returns
immediately without showing dialogs or terminating the process.
Called with 1 during process termination in DisplayCriticalError.

Parameters:
- dwDisable (uint): Non-zero to disable error handling

Returns:
- void

functions.name: _SmackFrameRate@4
functions.comment:
Sets the default frame rate for Smacker video playback.

Algorithm:
1. Check if nFramesPerSecond is positive (valid FPS value)
2. If positive: Calculate frame interval as -100000 / nFramesPerSecond
   - The negative value represents microseconds-per-frame for timing
3. If zero or negative: Store value directly as raw timing interval
4. Store result in g_nDefaultFrameRate global

Parameters:
  nFramesPerSecond (int) - Target frames per second for playback.
    - Positive values: Interpreted as FPS, converted to timing interval
    - Zero or negative: Used directly as raw timing value

Returns:
  void

Magic Numbers:
  0xFFFE7960 (-100000) - Microsecond conversion factor for frame timing

Related Functions:
  _SmackOpen@12 - Reads g_nDefaultFrameRate to set initial playback rate

functions.name: _SmackSoundOnOff@8
functions.comment:
Controls sound playback state for Smacker video audio tracks.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSmack pointer - return 0 if NULL
2. Check if sound is initialized (offset 0x444 != -1) - return 1 if uninitialized
3. If dwOnOffFlags is non-zero (turn ON):
   a. If sound already on, iterate through 7 audio channels
   b. Lock each channel buffer via DirectSound
   c. Calculate silence fill pattern (0x00 or 0x80 based on format)
   d. Fill unused buffer regions with silence pattern using REP STOSD/STOSB
   e. Update track position and byte counters
   f. Call user callback g_pfnSoundOnCallback if set
   g. Release DirectSound buffer locks
   h. Clear sound-on flag when complete
4. If dwOnOffFlags is zero (turn OFF):
   a. Store current frame position for later resume
   b. Set sound-on flag to 1
   c. Reset all 7 channel track states
   d. For each active track, call user notify callback and reset positions

Parameters:
  pSmack - Pointer to Smack structure containing video/audio state
  dwOnOffFlags - Non-zero to turn sound ON, zero to turn sound OFF
                 Bit 31 (0x80000000) affects buffer fill behavior

Returns:
  0 - Failure (NULL pSmack pointer)
  1 - Success (sound state changed or already in requested state)

Magic Numbers:
  0x444 - Smack structure sound initialized flag offset
  0x44c - Smack structure sound-on state flag offset
  0x374 - Current frame position offset
  0x50c - Saved frame position offset
  0x428 - Start of channel pointer array (7 channels, 4 bytes each)
  0x80  - 8-bit PCM silence value (128)
  0x00  - 16-bit PCM silence value (0)

functions.name: _SmackClose@4
functions.comment:
Closes and deallocates a Smack video/audio handle and all associated resources.

Algorithm:
1. Validate handle is not null - return immediately if null
2. If debug mode enabled (g_bDebugAudio == 1), output handle address to debug console via OutputDebugStringA
3. If audio tracks are initialized (pSmack->dwAudioInitFlag != -1):
   a. Iterate through 7 audio track buffer slots at offsets 0x428-0x440
   b. For each non-null slot: unlink from callback list via g_pfnUnlinkListNodeCallback
   c. Free nested buffer pointed to by track buffer via SmackFree
   d. Free the audio track buffer itself via SmackFree
   e. Decrement global audio buffer reference count (g_dwProgressCallbackCount)
   f. Mark audio tracks as uninitialized (set dwAudioInitFlag to -1)
4. If global reference count reaches 0 and shared buffer exists, free g_pSmackAudioBuffer
5. Close file handle via CloseHandle if valid (!= -1) and not externally managed (SMACK_FILEHANDLE flag not set)
6. Free individual buffers if non-null: pFrameBuffer2, pFrameBuffer1, pPaletteBuffer, pHuffmanTables, pExtraBuffer
7. Save dwFlags before zeroing structure
8. Zero entire handle structure using REP STOSD (0x144 dwords = 0x510 bytes)
9. Free handle memory via SmackFree unless SMACK_DONT_FREE_HANDLE flag (0x2000000) is set

Parameters:
pSmack - Pointer to Smack handle structure to close (Smack*)

Returns:
void - No return value

Special Cases:
- Null handle check prevents null pointer dereference
- SMACK_FILEHANDLE flag (0x1000 in dwFlags) prevents closing externally provided file handles
- SMACK_DONT_FREE_HANDLE flag (0x2000000 in dwFlags) prevents freeing the handle itself

Structure Layout (Smack Handle - key fields):
Offset   Size  Field              Description
0x390    4     dwFlags            Handle flags (SMACK_FILEHANDLE, SMACK_DONT_FREE_HANDLE, etc.)
0x3B0    4     hFile              File handle for Smack file (-1 if invalid)
0x3B8    4     pFrameBuffer1      First frame buffer pointer
0x3BC    4     pFrameBuffer2      Second frame buffer pointer
0x3D0    4     pHuffmanTables     Huffman decompression tables
0x3E0    4     pPaletteBuffer     Palette data buffer
0x428    28    apAudioTrackBufs   Array of 7 audio track buffer pointers (4 bytes each)
0x444    4     dwAudioInitFlag    Audio initialization state (-1 = not initialized)
0x450    4     pExtraBuffer       Additional buffer pointer

functions.name: ProcessSmackFrame
functions.comment:
Processes a single Smacker video frame with audio synchronization and palette conversion.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSmack pointer, return 0 if null
2. Check if frame is already being processed (offset 0x3a8), return 0 if busy
3. Get current time via timeGetTime() and initialize timing fields
4. If first frame, store initial timestamp at offset 0x490
5. If audio enabled (offset 0x68), copy audio buffer pointer
6. Increment frame counter at offset 0x49c
7. Process audio tracks via ProcessSmackAudioTracks()
8. If sound buffer active (offset 0x424):
   - Check buffer readiness via CheckSoundBufferReady()
   - If SMACK_NOSYNC flag (0x400) not set, compute skip decision
9. If frame data pointer valid (offset 0x3bc) and not skipping:
   - Set frame active flag at offset 0x408
   - If palette destination valid (offset 0x3c8):
     - Convert palette based on format byte:
       - 0x80 (-128): RGB24 to RGB555
       - 0xC0 (-64): RGB24 to RGB565
     - Copy 512 bytes (128 DWORDs) of palette to global buffer
   - Decode frame via DecodeSmackerFrame()
10. If skipping frame, increment skip counter at offset 0x4a0
11. Invoke progress callback if registered
12. Return sound buffer status

Parameters:
  pSmack - Pointer to Smack structure containing video/audio state

Returns:
  uint - Sound buffer status (0 = not ready or error, non-zero = ready)

Magic Numbers:
  0x80 (cPaletteFormat) - RGB555 palette format identifier
  0xC0 (cPaletteFormat) - RGB565 palette format identifier
  0x400 (flags) - SMACK_NOSYNC flag, disables audio sync wait
  0x80 (loop) - 128 DWORDs = 512 bytes palette size

Structure Offsets (Smack):
  Offset   | Size | Description
  0x68     | 4    | Audio buffer pointer (non-zero if audio enabled)
  0x6c     | var  | RGB24 palette source data
  0x374    | 4    | Audio buffer copy source
  0x390    | 4    | Flags field (bit 10 = NOSYNC)
  0x3a8    | 4    | Busy/processing flag
  0x3b8    | 4    | Decoder source buffer
  0x3bc    | 4    | Frame data pointer
  0x3c4    | 4    | Palette conversion enabled flag
  0x3c8    | 4    | Palette destination pointer
  0x3d8    | 4    | Audio buffer copy destination
  0x404    | 4    | Decoder destination buffer
  0x408    | 4    | Frame active flag (set to 1 during decode)
  0x424    | 4    | Sound buffer handle (non-zero if active)
  0x484    | 4    | Last frame timestamp
  0x488    | 4    | Current frame timestamp
  0x490    | 4    | First frame timestamp (initialized once)
  0x49c    | 4    | Frame counter
  0x4a0    | 4    | Skipped frame counter

functions.name: ProcessSmackAudioTracks
functions.comment:
Processes audio track data for the current Smack video frame.

Algorithm:
  1. Check if frame playback is active (FrameNum != -1) and not paused (field 0x44c == 0)
  2. Set AudioStarted flag to 1 if sound is enabled (field 0x424 != 0)
  3. Update timing accumulators on SmackBuffer at offset [0x428 + FrameNum*4]:
     - Add TimePerFrame (0x1c) to TimeAccumLow (0x20) and TimeAccumHigh (0x28)
     - If TimeAccumLow > 0xFA00000 (262M) and TimeAccumHigh > 0x2000000 (33M):
       Wrap by subtracting 0xFA00000 and adding 0x3E800 (256000) to TimeElapsed (0x24)
  4. Get active audio tracks bitmask from Smack+0x390
  5. For each active track (via FindFirstSetBitAndClear):
     a. Get track data pointer from Smack+0x3E8+track*4
     b. Calculate data size: if compressed (flag 0x80000000), use [data+4]; else use [data]-4
     c. Set "no data" flag in SmackBuffer+0x4c based on data size == 0
     d. Call progress callback if registered (g_dwProgressCallbackCount != 0)
     e. Clamp data size to available buffer space (SmackBuffer[6] - SmackBuffer[4])
     f. Handle buffer wrap: fill silence (0x00 or 0x80 for unsigned) if lookahead enabled
     g. Copy track data to circular buffer (or decompress via DecompressSmackFrame if compressed)
     h. Update buffer position pointers and wrap if needed
  6. After all tracks processed, check timing overflow and reset accumulators if needed

Parameters:
  pSmack (Smack*) - Pointer to the Smack video structure containing frame and audio data

Returns:
  void

SSA Temporaries (decompiler-generated, cannot be renamed):
  iVar1        - Frame index, later repurposed as SmackBuffer pointer (int)
  puVar2       - SmackBuffer pointer for current audio track (uint*)
  bVar3/bVar4  - Silence fill byte / track index (byte)
  uVar5-uVar8  - Loop counters, data size, byte counts (uint)
  pbVar9/11    - Source/destination byte pointers (byte*)
  puVar10      - Write position pointer (uint*)

Special Cases:
  - Early exit if FrameNum == -1 (no active playback)
  - Early exit if paused (field 0x44c != 0)
  - Handles circular buffer wrap-around for audio data
  - Fills silence bytes (0x00 for signed, 0x80 for unsigned audio) when lookahead enabled
  - Compressed audio (flag 0x80000000) uses DecompressSmackFrame for decompression

SmackBuffer Layout:
  Offset | Size | Field          | Description
  -------|------|----------------|----------------------------------
  0x00   | 4    | pBufferStart   | Start of circular buffer
  0x04   | 4    | pBufferEnd     | End of circular buffer
  0x0C   | 4    | pWritePos      | Current write position
  0x10   | 4    | dwBytesWritten | Total bytes written to buffer
  0x18   | 4    | dwBufferSize   | Total buffer size in bytes
  0x24   | 4    | dwSilenceBytes | Bytes of silence written
  0x2C   | 4    | dwTotalBytes   | Running total of all bytes processed
  0x30   | 4    | dwOverflowCnt  | Buffer overflow counter
  0x34   | 4    | dwPadCount     | Silence padding counter
  0x38   | 4    | dwLookahead    | Lookahead bytes threshold
  0x4C   | 4    | bNoData        | Flag: no data available for track
  0x50   | 4    | bIsUnsigned    | Flag: audio is unsigned (silence=0x80)
  0x58   | 4    | bPadEnabled    | Silence padding enabled
  0x5C   | 4    | bPadActive     | Silence padding currently active

Magic Numbers:
  0xFA00000  - Timing threshold (262,144,000) for accumulator wrap
  0x2000000  - Secondary timing threshold (33,554,432)
  0x3E800    - Time increment value (256,000)
  0x80000000 - Compressed audio flag (bit 31)
  0xFF       - Track index terminator (no more tracks)

functions.name: CheckSoundBufferReady
functions.comment:
Checks if the current Smack sound buffer is ready for processing.

Algorithm:
  1. Load sound index from Smack+0x444 (dwCurrentSound)
  2. Verify index is valid (not 0xFFFFFFFF) and processing flag at +0x44c is clear
  3. If override flag at +0x448 is clear, return success immediately
  4. Lookup sound buffer from table at Smack+0x428[index]
  5. Check buffer processing state at buffer+0x4c
  6. Call g_pfnGetSoundSize() to get current playback position
  7. Calculate total position: (buffer+0x28 >> 0xa (10)) + buffer+0x24
  8. Compare against size; if within bounds, clear override flag and return success

Parameters:
  pSmack  Pointer to Smack structure (via stack at +0x4)

Returns:
  uint combined value:
    - Low byte (AL): 1 = success/ready, 0 = failure/busy
    - Upper 24 bits: Current sound byte offset (from index or GetSoundSize)

Special Cases:
  - Invalid index (0xFFFFFFFF): Returns 0 (failure)
  - Processing flag set at +0x44c: Returns 0 (failure)
  - Buffer busy (buffer+0x4c != 0): Returns byte offset with AL=0
  - Override flag clear: Fast path returns success immediately

Structure Layout (Smack):
  Offset | Size | Field             | Type   | Description
  0x428  | var  | aSoundBuffers     | DWORD* | Array of sound buffer pointers
  0x444  | 4    | dwCurrentSound    | DWORD  | Current sound index (-1 = none)
  0x448  | 4    | dwOverrideFlag    | DWORD  | Priority/processing override
  0x44c  | 4    | dwProcessingFlag  | DWORD  | Active processing indicator

Structure Layout (SoundBuffer):
  Offset | Size | Field             | Type   | Description
  0x24   | 4    | dwPositionOffset  | DWORD  | Base position offset
  0x28   | 4    | dwDurationBits    | DWORD  | Duration (bits 10-31) + offset (bits 0-9)
  0x4c   | 4    | dwBusyState       | DWORD  | Non-zero if buffer is being processed

functions.name: _SmackSummary@8
functions.comment:
Populates a summary structure with Smack video playback statistics.

Gathers timing data, frame counts, and performance metrics from the Smack
structure and writes them into the output summary array.

Algorithm:
1. Accumulate frame timing statistics via AccumulateFrameTimingStats
2. Get current time and calculate elapsed playback time
3. Copy frame counts, timing stats, and buffer sizes to summary array
4. Calculate average frame rate (frames per 1000ms) if total time > 0
5. Copy audio timing and synchronization data
6. Retrieve current audio track information if available

Parameters:
  pSmack - Pointer to Smack video structure containing playback state
  pnSummary - Output array receiving 19 summary statistics values

Returns:
  void

Summary Array Layout (indices):
  [0]  Elapsed time since playback start (ms)
  [1]  Total frames decoded
  [2]  Video decode time (ms)
  [3]  Blit/render time (ms)
  [4]  Read time (ms)
  [5]  Current audio track sample offset
  [6]  Audio decode time (ms)
  [7]  Frames behind schedule
  [8]  Frame skip count
  [9]  Audio buffer fill time
  [10] Average frame rate (frames per 1000ms)
  [11] Audio rate or default 1000
  [12] Video rate or default 1000
  [13] Audio frames decoded + 1
  [14] Video frames decoded + 1
  [15] Audio buffer underruns
  [16] Video buffer underruns
  [17] Highest frame memory usage
  [18] Audio buffer high watermark

functions.name: AccumulateFrameTimingStats
functions.comment:
Accumulates frame timing statistics for Smack video playback profiling.

Algorithm:
  1. If frame timing started (offset 0x484 != 0):
     a. Get current time via timeGetTime()
     b. Calculate elapsed frame time = currentTime - frameStartTime
     c. Clear frame start timestamp (0x484 = 0)
     d. Update slowest frame tracking:
        - If elapsed > slowest time (0x4ac): shift slowest to second, record new slowest
        - Else if elapsed > second slowest (0x4b0): update second slowest
  2. If decompress timing started (offset 0x48c != 0):
     a. Get current time (reuse if already fetched)
     b. Add elapsed time to decompress accumulator (0x4a4)
     c. Clear decompress start timestamp
  3. If blit timing started (offset 0x488 != 0):
     a. Get current time (reuse if already fetched)
     b. Add elapsed time to blit accumulator (0x4a8)
     c. Clear blit start timestamp

Parameters:
  pSmk - Pointer to Smack video structure containing timing fields

Returns:
  void - Updates timing statistics in-place within Smack structure

Structure Offsets (relative to pSmk):
  Offset | Size | Field                  | Description
  -------|------|------------------------|----------------------------------
  0x374  | 4    | dwCurrentFrame         | Current frame number
  0x484  | 4    | dwFrameStartTime       | Frame start timestamp (ms)
  0x488  | 4    | dwBlitStartTime        | Blit start timestamp (ms)
  0x48c  | 4    | dwDecompressStartTime  | Decompress start timestamp (ms)
  0x4a4  | 4    | dwTotalDecompressTime  | Accumulated decompress time (ms)
  0x4a8  | 4    | dwTotalBlitTime        | Accumulated blit time (ms)
  0x4ac  | 4    | dwSlowestFrameTime     | Slowest frame elapsed time (ms)
  0x4b0  | 4    | dwSecondSlowestTime    | Second slowest frame time (ms)
  0x4b4  | 4    | dwSlowestFrameNum      | Frame number of slowest frame
  0x4b8  | 4    | dwSecondSlowestNum     | Frame number of second slowest

functions.name: _SmackNextFrame@4
functions.comment:
Advances a Smack video to the next frame.

Algorithm:
1. Return early if pSmk is NULL
2. If video is paused (offset 0x3a8 != 0), increment frame counter and return
3. Call progress callback if registered (g_pfnSmackSoundInit)
4. Accumulate timing statistics for the current frame
5. Read frame size from frame size table at offset 0x3dc indexed by current frame
6. Increment frame index at offset 0x374
7. Add frame size to cumulative data offset at 0x3d4
8. If more frames remain (frame index < total frames at offset 0xc), read next frame data
9. Decompress the current frame
10. Call progress callback again if registered

Parameters:
  pSmk - Smack * - Pointer to Smack video structure

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - NULL pSmk returns immediately without processing
  - Paused state (offset 0x3a8 != 0) only increments frame counter

Structure Offsets:
  Offset   Size  Field              Description
  0x00c    4     dwFrameCount       Total number of frames in video
  0x374    4     dwCurrentFrame     Current frame index (0-based)
  0x3a8    4     dwPauseFlag        Non-zero when video is paused
  0x3d4    4     dwDataOffset       Cumulative byte offset into video data
  0x3dc    4     pFrameSizeTable    Pointer to array of frame sizes (uint[dwFrameCount])

functions.name: RenderSmackFrameToScreen
functions.signature: void RenderSmackFrameToScreen(int pSmack, dword dwSrcPitch, int nSrcYOffset, int nDestWidth, int nPaletteTable, int nPaletteOffset, dword dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Renders a Smack video frame to the screen with scaling and palette support.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSmack is non-null; return early if null
2. Handle 320-width (0x140) special case: force palette base 0xa0000, offset 0
3. If previous blit context exists at pSmack+0x3bc:
   a. Preserve palette data pointer from pSmack+0x3c8
   b. If context type==1, save stride and buffer data pointer
   c. Adjust allocation tracking at pSmack+0x480
4. Extract scale mode flags from pSmack+0x390:
   - 0x100000: Double width mode (width*2, height/2)
   - 0x200000: Interlaced mode (width*2, height/2, 8x multiplier)
5. Calculate display list buffer size based on frame dimensions and scale
6. Allocate display list buffer via FUN_10004c80
7. Initialize display list header:
   - Byte 0: Type marker (0)
   - Byte 1: Interlace flag
   - Byte 2: Alpha/transparency value from dwFlags high byte
8. Copy palette data (0x200 bytes) if previous palette exists
9. Build display list entries via FUN_10006a90:
   - Handle 64KB segment boundary crossings
   - Generate bank switch commands (0xfffe, 0xfffd, 0xffff)
   - Track palette indices per segment
10. Terminate display list with 0xffff marker
11. Clean up previous context via ApplyPresetUnitTileAttributes

Parameters:
  pSmack: Pointer to Smack video structure containing frame data
  dwSrcPitch: Source pitch (bytes per row), aligned to 4-byte boundary
  nSrcYOffset: Y offset into source frame for partial blits
  nDestWidth: Destination width (320=0x140 triggers special mode)
  nPaletteTable: Base address of palette lookup table
  nPaletteOffset: Offset into palette table
  dwFlags: Bit flags controlling rendering:
    - Bits 30-31 (0xc0000000): Palette mode selector
    - Bits 24-29: Alpha/transparency value

Returns: void (modifies Smack structure in place)

Special Cases:
  - 320-width mode: Forces VGA palette base (0xa0000), clears offset
  - Null pSmack: Early return with no operation
  - 64KB boundary: Generates bank switch display commands

Magic Numbers:
  0x140 (320): Standard VGA width, triggers compatibility mode
  0xa0000: VGA video memory base address
  0x3bc: Offset to blit context pointer in Smack structure
  0x3c8: Offset to palette data pointer in Smack structure
  0x390: Offset to render flags in Smack structure
  0x100000: Double-width scaling flag
  0x200000: Interlaced rendering flag
  0x200: Palette data size (512 bytes)
  0x400: Palette table offset in display list
  0x600: Base header size for display list
  0xfffe: Bank switch command (continue next segment)
  0xfffd: Interlace sync command
  0xffff: End of display list marker

functions.name: BuildVertexTransformMatrix
functions.signature: void BuildVertexTransformMatrix(short * pnTransformBuffer, short nScaleX, uint dwScaleFactors, short nOffsetY, short nOffsetX, short nShearY)
functions.comment:
Builds a 5-element transformation matrix for vertex coordinate scaling and shearing.

Algorithm:
  1. Store primary scale factor (nScaleX) in element[0]
  2. Calculate normalized scale divisor (dwScaleFactors >> 2) for element[1]
  3. Compute sheared Y offset (nOffsetY * nScaleX - 4 * nShearY) for element[2]
  4. Compute linear Y offset (nOffsetY * nScaleX) for element[3]
  5. Calculate skewed X offset with cross-term (nOffsetX * nScaleX - dwScaleFactors * nShearY) for element[4]

Parameters:
  pnTransformBuffer - Pointer to short[5] output array for transformation values
  nScaleX           - Primary scaling factor for X dimension
  dwScaleFactors    - Bit-packed scale values (right-shifted by 2 for normalization)
  nOffsetY          - Y-axis translation offset
  nOffsetX          - X-axis translation offset
  nShearY           - Shear/skew factor (applied with 4x multiplier)

Returns:
  void - Populates pnTransformBuffer[0..4] with transformation coefficients

Output Buffer Layout:
  Offset  Element  Formula                              Purpose
  0x00    [0]      nScaleX                              Primary scale factor
  0x02    [1]      dwScaleFactors >> 2                  Normalized scale divisor
  0x04    [2]      nOffsetY * nScaleX - 4 * nShearY     Sheared Y offset
  0x06    [3]      nOffsetY * nScaleX                   Linear Y offset
  0x08    [4]      nOffsetX * nScaleX - dwScaleFactors * nShearY  Cross-term X offset

Called By:
  RenderSmackFrameToScreen - Sets up transformation for Smacker video frame rendering

functions.name: _SmackToBuffer@28
functions.signature: void _SmackToBuffer@28(int pSmack, uint dwLeftOffset, uint dwTopOffset, uint dwPitch, uint dwDestHeight, byte * pDestBuffer, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Configures and initializes the Smacker video playback buffer for rendering.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSmack pointer, early exit if NULL
2. If pDestBuffer is NULL (cleanup mode):
   a. Free existing buffer via ApplyPresetUnitTileAttributes
   b. Update memory tracking and clear buffer pointer
   c. Return early
3. Calculate adjusted dimensions based on scaling flags:
   - 0x100000: Horizontal scaling (halve height, double pitch)
   - 0x200000: Vertical scaling (set pixel mode to 7, halve height)
4. Determine bytes per pixel (1 or 2) based on dwFlags high bits
5. Calculate required buffer size via CalcSmackerBufferOffset
6. Allocate or reuse existing buffer:
   - If buffer exists but is too small, free it first
   - Allocate new buffer via FUN_10004c80
   - Zero-initialize the new buffer
7. Set up palette transfer area if scaling enabled (512 bytes at buffer end)
8. Copy previous palette data if it exists
9. Configure SmackBuffer header structure:
   - Offset +0x00: Valid flag (1)
   - Offset +0x01: Vertical scale flag
   - Offset +0x02: Scale factor from dwFlags high byte
   - Offset +0x04: Destination pointer calculation
   - Offset +0x08: Width in DWORDs
   - Offset +0x0C: Height in DWORDs
   - Offset +0x10-0x1C: Row stride calculations (depends on flip flag)
   - Offset +0x24: Frame width
   - Offset +0x28: Adjusted height
10. Free old buffer if it was replaced

Parameters:
  pSmack (Smack *): Pointer to Smacker video handle structure
  dwLeftOffset (uint): Horizontal offset in destination buffer (pixels)
  dwTopOffset (uint): Vertical offset in destination buffer (pixels)
  dwPitch (uint): Destination buffer stride in bytes
  dwDestHeight (uint): Total height of destination buffer
  pDestBuffer (byte *): Destination surface pointer, or NULL to free buffer
  dwFlags (uint): Rendering flags:
    - Bit 0 (0x01): Flip vertically
    - Bits 30-31: Scale mode (0=no extra palette, else reserve 512 bytes)
    - Bits 24-31: Scale factor value

Returns:
  void - Buffer configuration stored in Smack structure at offsets:
    +0x3BC: Pointer to SmackBuffer
    +0x3C0: Buffer size
    +0x3C8: Palette area pointer
    +0x394: Left offset cache
    +0x398: Top offset cache

Special Cases:
  - NULL pSmack: Returns immediately
  - NULL pDestBuffer: Cleanup mode, frees existing buffer
  - Existing buffer too small: Reallocates

Magic Numbers Reference:
  0x3BC - SmackBuffer pointer offset in Smack structure
  0x3C0 - Buffer size offset
  0x3C8 - Palette pointer offset
  0x390 - Flags offset (scaling modes)
  0x394 - Cached left offset
  0x398 - Cached top offset
  0x480 - Memory tracking offset
  0x100000 - Horizontal scaling flag
  0x200000 - Vertical scaling flag
  0xC0000000 - Scale mode mask
  0x200 - Palette buffer size (512 bytes)
  0x80 - Palette DWORD count (128 entries)

functions.name: _SmackColorTrans@8
functions.comment:
Applies color translation/palette remapping to a Smack video handle.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSmack pointer is non-null
2. If progress callback is registered, invoke it (pre-operation notification)
3. Extract internal Smack structure from offset 0x3B8 of the handle
4. Call SmackRemapFramePalettes to apply palette translation
5. If progress callback is registered, invoke it (post-operation notification)

Parameters:
  pSmack    - Pointer to Smack video handle containing video state
  pbPalette - Pointer to 256-entry palette array (768 bytes RGB or 1024 bytes RGBA)

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  - If pSmack is NULL, function returns immediately without any processing
  - Progress callbacks at g_pfnSmackSoundInit are invoked before and after remapping
    if g_dwProgressCallbackCount is non-zero

Structure Access:
  Offset    Size  Field                 Description
  0x3B8     4     pInternalSmack        Pointer to internal Smack structure for remapping

functions.name: _SmackColorRemap@16
functions.signature: void _SmackColorRemap@16(int nSmackHandle, uint dwPalette, uint dwPaletteSize, uint dwFlags)
functions.comment:
Creates a color remap table by finding closest matching colors between source and destination palettes.

Algorithm:
1. Early exit if pSmackHandle is NULL (video handle required)
2. Call optional callback function at [0x10015e88] if [0x10014298] is set (pre-remap hook)
3. Clamp dwPaletteSize to maximum of 256 entries
4. Initialize channel offsets based on dwFlags:
   - Bit 2 (0x4): BGR byte order instead of RGB
   - Bit 3 (0x8): Combine with bit 2 for alternate component ordering
   - Bit 1 (0x2): Swap red/green channel offsets
   - Bit 0 (0x1): Double all offsets (16-bit color mode)
5. For each of 256 palette indices:
   a. Extract source RGB components from internal palette at [pSmackHandle+0x6c]
   b. For each entry in destination palette (pbPalette):
      - Calculate squared difference for each RGB channel
      - Sum squared differences for total color distance
      - Track minimum distance and best matching index
   c. Store best match index in remap table (256-byte array at ESP+0x54)
6. Call SmackRemapFramePalettes(pSmackHandle+0x3b8, remapTable) to apply remap

Parameters:
pSmackHandle - Pointer to Smack video handle structure containing internal palette at offset 0x6c
               and frame palette pointer at offset 0x3b8
pbPalette    - Pointer to source palette data (RGB triplets, byte array)
dwPaletteSize - Number of palette entries to process (clamped to 256 max)
dwFlags      - Color format flags controlling channel order and bit depth

Returns:
void - No return value; updates internal remap table via SmackRemapFramePalettes

Magic Numbers:
0x100 (256) - Maximum palette entries
0x6c  (108) - Offset to internal palette in Smack handle
0x3b8 (952) - Offset to frame palette pointer in Smack handle
0x4, 0x8, 0x2, 0x1 - Flag bits for color format configuration

functions.name: _SmackGetTrackData@12
functions.comment:
Retrieves audio track data from the current Smack video frame.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSmack pointer is non-null
2. Check if Smack structure is in valid state (offset 0x3a8 must be 0)
3. Call FindFirstSetBitAndClear on track request flags to get track index
4. Validate track index is in range 0-6 (Smacker supports up to 7 audio tracks)
5. Get track data pointer from track array at pSmack+0x3e8 (offset 1000)
6. Check track flags at pSmack+0x48+(trackIndex*4) for compression bit 0x80000000
7. If compressed (bit set):
   a. Allocate 0x2000 byte audio buffer if g_pSmackAudioBuffer is null
   b. Call DecompressSmackFrame to decompress audio to destination
   c. Return compressed size from trackData[1]
8. If uncompressed (bit clear):
   a. Get data size from trackData[0]
   b. Skip if size is 3 or 4 (header only, no payload)
   c. Copy (size-4) bytes from trackData+4 to destination buffer
   d. Return (size-4) as bytes copied

Parameters:
  pSmack      - Pointer to Smack video structure handle
  pDestBuffer - Pointer to destination buffer for audio data output

Returns:
  uint - Number of bytes written to pDestBuffer on success
  0    - On failure (null handle, invalid state, invalid track, alloc failure)

Special Cases:
  Returns 0 if pSmack is null
  Returns 0 if Smack state at offset 0x3a8 is non-zero (busy/invalid)
  Returns 0 if track index exceeds 6
  Returns 0 if track data pointer is null
  Returns 0 if audio buffer allocation fails

Magic Numbers:
  0x3a8 - Smack state/lock flag offset
  0x3e8 (1000) - Track data pointer array offset
  0x48 - Track flags array offset
  0x80000000 - Compression flag bit in track flags
  0x2000 - Audio decompression buffer size (8KB)

functions.name: _SmackToBufferRect@8
functions.signature: int _SmackToBufferRect@8(int nUnused1, int nUnused2, int pSmk, int nFlags)
functions.comment:
Retrieves the next dirty rectangle from the Smack video frame's update queue.

This function is part of the Smacker video codec's dirty rectangle tracking system.
It processes the queue of screen regions that have changed during video decoding and
returns coordinate information for the next rectangle to be redrawn.

Algorithm:
1. Validate pSmk pointer - return 0 if null
2. Initialize timing if first call (timestamp at offset 0x48c)
3. Update elapsed time tracking (offsets 0x488, 0x4a8)
4. Check if buffer update mode is active (offset 0x408)
5. If active and nFlags != 2, process dirty rect queue:
   - Call ComputeSmackBufferRect to validate rectangles
   - Remove invalid entries via RemoveArrayElementCompact
   - Continue until queue count less than 16 or no more removals
6. Return 0 if queue is empty
7. Pop next rectangle from queue (decrement count at 0x4c8)
8. Copy rectangle coordinates to output fields:
   - Offset 0x380: Left (X)
   - Offset 0x384: Top (Y)
   - Offset 0x388: Width
   - Offset 0x38c: Height
9. Shift remaining queue entries forward (memcpy via MOVSD)
10. Return 1 to indicate rectangle was retrieved

Parameters:
  nUnused1 (ECX): Unused fastcall register parameter
  nUnused2 (EDX): Unused fastcall register parameter  
  pSmk: Pointer to Smack video structure
  nFlags: Rendering flags (2 = skip processing)

Returns:
  1: Rectangle coordinates copied to pSmk output fields
  0: No rectangles available or invalid state

  DVar1 (dwTimestamp): Return value from timeGetTime()
  iVar2 (nPrevTime/nComputeResult): Previous timestamp or rect validation result
  uVar3 (dwQueueIndex/dwCopyCount): Queue byte offset or copy loop counter
  pcbArraySize (pdwRectCount): Pointer to queue count at Smk+0x4c8
  puVar4 (pdwSrc): Source pointer for queue shift copy
  puVar5 (pdwDst): Destination pointer for queue shift copy
  extraout_ECX/EDX: Clobbered register values after function calls

Structure Layout (Smack offsets used):
  Offset   Size  Field              Description
  0x380    4     nOutLeft           Output: rectangle left X
  0x384    4     nOutTop            Output: rectangle top Y
  0x388    4     nOutWidth          Output: rectangle width
  0x38c    4     nOutHeight         Output: rectangle height
  0x408    4     bBufferActive      Buffer update mode flag
  0x488    4     dwPrevTimestamp    Previous timing value
  0x48c    4     dwTimestamp        Current timing (timeGetTime)
  0x4a8    4     dwElapsedAccum     Accumulated elapsed time
  0x4c8    4     nRectQueueCount    Number of rects in queue (x4)
  0x4cc    64    aRectQueue[16]     Rectangle queue array (4 dwords each)
  0x4dc    ...   ...                Extended queue storage

functions.name: ComputeSmackBufferRect
functions.signature: int ComputeSmackBufferRect(dword dwUnused1, dword dwUnused2, dword pSmackCtx, int nMode, dword * pOutputRect)
functions.comment:
Computes the output rectangle bounds for Smack video buffer rendering.

This function implements a state machine that processes Smack video blocks
and calculates the visible dirty rectangle for partial screen updates.

Algorithm:
1. Check state at offset 0x408 in context structure
2. If state == 3: Reset state to 0 and return 0 (done)
3. If state == 1: Call SmackDecompressNextBlock to decode first block
4. If decompress fails with no data at offset 0x68: return 0
5. Otherwise transition state to 2 and continue processing
6. State 2: Accumulate block bounds across multiple decompress calls
7. Mode 0: Calculate rect size and clamp to available buffer
8. Mode 1: Simple accumulation loop until decompress complete
9. Apply 8-byte alignment to X coordinates for SIMD optimization
10. Write final rect (x1, y1, x2, y2) to output array

Parameters:
  dwUnused1 (ECX) - Unused register parameter (preserved for calling convention)
  dwUnused2 (EDX) - Unused register parameter (preserved for calling convention)
  pSmackCtx       - Pointer to Smack context structure containing video state
  nMode           - Processing mode: 0 = size-limited, 1 = full accumulation
  pOutputRect     - Output array of 4 dwords [x1, y1, x2, y2] for dirty rect

Returns:
  1 - Success, pOutputRect contains valid dirty rectangle
  0 - No data to process or end of frame reached

Structure Offsets in pSmackCtx:
  +0x004: Video width limit
  +0x068: Frame data available flag
  +0x390: Video flags (bit 0x300000 = double resolution)
  +0x394: X offset base
  +0x398: Y offset base
  +0x3BC: Decompressor context pointer
  +0x408: State machine (0=init, 1=first, 2=processing, 3=done)
  +0x40C: Current block X position
  +0x410: Current block Y position  
  +0x414: Block width
  +0x418: Block height

functions.name: RemoveArrayElementCompact
functions.signature: void RemoveArrayElementCompact(int * pArray, uint dwMatchIndex, uint * pcbArraySize)
functions.comment:
Removes an element from a compact array by finding matching field patterns and shifting remaining elements.

This function searches the array for elements that share field values with the element at dwMatchIndex.
When a match is found based on specific field comparison patterns, it copies the differing field value
from the matched element to the current element, then compacts the array by removing the matched element.

Algorithm:
1. Initialize loop index to 0, scan from beginning of array
2. Skip comparison if current index equals match index
3. Compare current element against match element using two field patterns:
   - Pattern 1: field0 and field2 match, then check field1/field3 cross-match
   - Pattern 2: field1 and field3 match, then check field0/field2 cross-match
4. On match found, copy the differing field value from match to current element
5. Shift all elements after dwMatchIndex left by one position using REP MOVSD
6. Decrement array size by 4 (one element worth of indices)
7. Restart scan from beginning with updated array

Parameters:
    pArray       - Pointer to CompactArrayElement array to modify
    dwMatchIndex - Index (in dwords, not elements) of target element to remove
    pcbArraySize - Pointer to array size counter (in dwords); decremented on removal

Returns:
    void - Array is modified in place; *pcbArraySize updated to reflect new size

Special Cases:
    - Empty array (size=0): Returns immediately without modification
    - No match found: Returns after full scan without modification
    - Match at current index: Skipped to avoid self-comparison

Structure Layout (CompactArrayElement, 16 bytes):
    Offset  Size  Field   Type    Description
    0x00    4     field0  dword   First comparison field
    0x04    4     field1  dword   Second comparison field
    0x08    4     field2  dword   Third comparison field
    0x0C    4     field3  dword   Fourth comparison field

Magic Numbers:
    0x10 (16)     - Element stride in bytes (4 dwords per element)
    0x04          - Index increment per element (dword-based indexing)
    0x3FFFFFFF    - Mask for shift count calculation (30-bit limit)

functions.name: _SmackSoundInTrack@8
functions.comment:
Checks if a Smack video has valid audio data in any of the specified tracks.

Algorithm:
1. Return 0 if pSmack is NULL
2. Loop through set bits in dwTrackMask (bits 13-19 represent tracks 0-6)
3. For each track, call FindFirstSetBitAndClear to get track index
4. Read track audio flags from pSmack->TrackFlags[trackIndex] at offset 0x48
5. Check if track has valid audio: bit 30 set AND lower 24 bits non-zero
6. Return 1 if valid track found, continue loop otherwise
7. Return 0 if no valid tracks remain in mask

Parameters:
  pSmack (Smack*) - Pointer to Smack video structure
  dwTrackMask (dword) - Bitmask of tracks to check (bits 13-19 = tracks 0-6)

Returns:
  1 - Valid audio data found in at least one specified track
  0 - No valid audio in any specified track, or pSmack is NULL

Magic Numbers:
  0xfe000 - Track bitmask (bits 13-19, 7 possible audio tracks)
  0x48 - Offset to TrackFlags array in Smack structure
  0x40000000 - Bit 30: Track has audio data flag
  0x00ffffff - Lower 24 bits: Audio data size/presence indicator

  uVar1 - dwTrackFlags: Audio flags for current track from Smack structure
  bVar2 - bTrackIndex: Track index (0-6) from FindFirstSetBitAndClear

functions.name: SmackVolumePan
functions.signature: void SmackVolumePan(int nSmackHandle, int nChannelMask, int nVolume, int nPan)
functions.comment:
Sets volume and pan for active Smack audio channels.

Iterates through the channel mask, processing each set bit to apply volume
and pan settings via the registered sound callback. Volume and pan values
are clamped to 0x10000 (65536) maximum.

Algorithm:
1. Validate nSmackHandle is non-null and has valid sound index (offset 0x444 != -1)
2. Clamp volume to maximum 0x10000
3. Clamp pan to maximum 0x10000
4. Extract channel bits from mask (bits 13-19, mask 0xFE000)
5. For each set channel bit:
   a. Call FindFirstSetBitAndClear to get channel index (0-6)
   b. Get sound handle from Smack structure at offset 0x428 + index*4
   c. If handle valid and callback registered, invoke callback with volume/pan

Parameters:
  nSmackHandle (int) - Pointer to Smack handle structure
  nChannelMask (int) - Bitmask of channels to modify (bits 13-19 for channels 0-6)
  nVolume (int) - Volume level (0 to 0x10000, clamped if higher)
  nPan (int) - Pan position (0 to 0x10000, clamped if higher)

Returns:
  void

Special Cases:
  - Returns immediately if nSmackHandle is NULL
  - Returns if sound index at offset 0x444 is -1 (invalid)
  - Skips channels with no sound handle
  - Skips if g_pfnSmackSoundCallback is NULL

Magic Numbers:
  0x10000 - Maximum volume/pan value (65536)
  0xFE000 - Channel mask filter (bits 13-19)
  0x444 - Offset in Smack structure for sound validity index
  0x428 - Offset in Smack structure for sound handle array base
  7 - Maximum channel index (channels 0-6)

Structure Layout (Smack sound-related offsets):
  Offset  Size  Field           Description
  0x428   4*7   paSoundHandles  Array of 7 sound handles for channels 0-6
  0x444   4     nSoundIndex     Sound validity index (-1 = invalid)

functions.name: _SmackWait@4
functions.comment:
Waits for the appropriate time to display the next Smacker video frame.

This function implements frame timing synchronization for Smacker video playback.
It checks whether the current time has reached the next scheduled frame time,
and if audio is active, synchronizes with audio buffer position.

Algorithm:
1. Return 0 if handle is NULL or video is stopped (offset +0x3a8)
2. Invoke sound progress callback if registered
3. If audio track is inactive (index == -1):
   a. Check frame ready flag at +0x41c
   b. Get current time from timeGetTime() and scale by 100
   c. If next frame time uninitialized (-1), set to current + interval
   d. If current time >= next frame time, advance timing and set ready flag
4. If audio track is active:
   a. Check audio is playing (+0x448) and not paused (+0x44c)
   b. Get audio playback position via sound callback
   c. Compare position against buffer threshold
   d. Clear audio playing flag when buffer exhausted
5. Call SmackReadFrame() when ready to advance

Parameters:
    pSmk - Pointer to Smacker video handle structure (Smack*)

Returns:
    1 - Frame was read, ready for display
    0 - Not yet time for next frame, or video stopped/paused

Structure Layout (Smacker handle offsets):
    +0x3a8  dwStopped       - Non-zero if playback stopped
    +0x41c  dwFrameReady    - Non-zero when frame timing satisfied
    +0x420  dwNextFrameTime - Scaled timestamp for next frame (ms * 100)
    +0x424  dwFrameInterval - Time between frames in scaled units
    +0x428  apAudioBufs[7]  - Array of audio buffer pointers (7 tracks)
    +0x444  nAudioTrack     - Active audio track index (-1 = none)
    +0x448  dwAudioPlaying  - Non-zero if audio is playing
    +0x44c  dwAudioPaused   - Non-zero if audio is paused

Magic Numbers:
    100 - Time scaling factor (milliseconds to internal units)
    0xFFFFFFFF (-1) - Uninitialized next frame time marker
    8 - Audio position margin for buffer comparison
    0x3FF (>>10) - Audio buffer size field extraction mask

functions.name: MemoryCopyRegions
functions.signature: byte * MemoryCopyRegions(byte * pbDest, byte * pbSrcEnd, byte * pbSrc, int iDestEnd, uint dwSize)
functions.comment:
Copies data from two memory regions into a destination buffer with wrap-around support.

Algorithm:
  1. Calculate bytes available in first region: iDestEnd - pbSrcEnd
  2. If bytes available is less than or equal to total size and non-zero:
     a. Copy dwBytesAvailable bytes from pbSrcEnd to pbDest using REP MOVSD/MOVSB
     b. Reduce remaining size by bytes copied
     c. Advance destination pointer
  3. If remaining bytes to copy (dwSize) is non-zero:
     a. Copy remaining bytes from pbSrc to current destination
     b. Use REP MOVSD for dwords, REP MOVSB for remainder
  4. Return pointer past end of copied data

Parameters:
  pbDest    - byte*  - Destination buffer start address
  pbSrcEnd  - byte*  - First source region pointer (typically buffer wrap point)
  pbSrc     - byte*  - Second source region pointer (typically buffer start)
  iDestEnd  - int    - End boundary of destination for size calculation
  dwSize    - uint   - Total number of bytes to copy across both regions

Returns:
  byte* - Pointer to position after last copied byte (end of written data)

Special Cases:
  - If dwBytesAvailable == 0, skips first region copy entirely
  - If dwSize == 0 after first copy, skips second region copy
  - Handles circular buffer wrap-around by splitting copy across two regions

Magic Numbers:
  0x2 (SHR 2)  - Divide by 4 to get dword count
  0x3 (AND 3)  - Mask to get remainder bytes (0-3)

Callers:
  UpdateAudioStreamBuffers, ProcessStreamQueue, ProcessSmackSoundQueue, ProcessSmackBufferList

functions.name: InitializeMssSoundSystem
strings: 0x14490|s_Smacker_needs_at_least_version_3_10014490|Smacker needs at least version 3.50F of MSS - playing without sound.
functions.comment:
Initializes the Miles Sound System (MSS) for Smacker video audio playback.
Loads MSS32.DLL dynamically, validates version compatibility, and imports
all required AIL (Audio Interface Library) function pointers for audio mixing.

Algorithm:
  1. Check if MSS is already initialized via g_pListHead, return false if so
  2. Store the Smacker handle in g_pSmackHandle for later use
  3. If MSS callback not set, load MSS32.DLL with error mode suppression
  4. Validate DLL handle is valid (must be >= 0x20, not error code)
  5. Load version string from DLL resource ID 1 into buffer
  6. Compare version against minimum required "3.50F" using __strcmpi
  7. If version too old, show error MessageBox and fail
  8. Import all AIL function pointers via GetProcAddress (22 functions)
  9. Check AIL_get_preference(15) to determine audio mode capability
  10. If preference returns 0, fall back to DirectSound via _SmackSoundUseDirectSound
  11. Set up internal callback function pointers for stream processing
  12. Set g_pfnSmackSoundCallback to internal MSS handler at LAB_10007d80

Parameters:
  pSmack - Pointer to Smack structure containing video/audio configuration.
           Field at offset 0x4C contains DirectSound fallback parameter.

Returns:
  true  - MSS initialized successfully or was already initialized with MSS
  false - Initialization failed (DLL load error, version mismatch, no audio)

Error Handling:
  SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS (0x8000) suppresses DLL load error dialogs.
  Version mismatch shows MessageBox with title "Smacker Version Error".
  On failure, FreeLibrary is called and g_hMss32Dll is set to NULL.

Magic Numbers:
  0x8000 - SEM_FAILCRITICALERRORS flag for SetErrorMode
  0x20   - Minimum valid HINSTANCE value (below are system error codes)
  0x0F   - AIL preference ID for checking audio capability
  0x40   - Buffer size for version string (64 bytes)
  0x4C   - Offset to DirectSound parameter in Smack structure

functions.name: ProcessStreamQueue
functions.comment:
Process all active stream buffers, copying pending data and managing queue state.

Algorithm:
  1. Load linked list head from g_pStreamQueueHead (global stream queue)
  2. For each stream in queue (iterate via [ESI+0x3C] next pointer):
     a. Call state query callback on stream handle (g_pfnQueryStreamState)
     b. If active, set stream flagged bit (offset 0x58)
     c. Check transfer conditions: data pending, state valid (< 2), etc.
     d. Call size query callback (g_pfnGetBufferState) to get buffer state (0 or 1)
     e. Align pending bytes: cbSize = size & 0xFFFFFFFC, cap to available
     f. If no timestamp set (offset 0x7C), call timeGetTime() and store
     g. Accumulate pending bytes to running total (offset 0x60)
     h. Copy data via MemoryCopyRegions from appropriate buffer
     i. Call update callback (g_pfnUpdateStreamBuffer) with buffer index and size
     j. Update position/size fields (offset 0x78, 0x10)
  3. After all streams processed, call cleanup callback (g_pfnCleanupQueue)

Parameters:
  (void) - No parameters. Operates on global stream queue g_pStreamQueueHead

Returns:
  void - Always succeeds, no return value

Structure Layout (stream element at ESI):
  Offset | Size | Field              | Type | Description
  0x0    | 4    | pData              | void*| Destination buffer pointer
  0x4    | 4    | cbRemaining        | uint | Bytes still to transfer
  0x8    | 4    | pSource            | void*| Source buffer pointer
  0x10   | 4    | dwState            | uint | Stream state/handle
  0x1D   | 4    | dwThreshold        | uint | Minimum before transfer
  0x1E   | 4    | cbPending          | uint | Bytes accumulated
  0x1F   | 4    | dwTimestamp        | DWORD| Last transfer time (via timeGetTime)
  0x20   | 4    | dwFlags            | uint | Control flags
  0x3C   | 4    | pNext              | ptr  | Next stream in linked list
  0x40   | 4    | dwHandle           | uint | Handle passed to callbacks
  0x44   | 4    | cbMaxTransfer      | uint | Max bytes per transfer (aligned)
  0x58   | 4    | dwFlaggedBit       | uint | Active stream marker
  0x60   | 4    | cbTransferred      | uint | Total bytes transferred
  0x74   | 4    | dwMinSize          | uint | Minimum data check (offset 0x1D field)
  0x78   | 4    | cbPendingDelta     | uint | Accumulation value
  0x7C   | 4    | dwTimeoutVal       | DWORD| Current timeout reference
  0x80   | 4    | dwFlagField        | uint | Condition flag

Special Cases:
  - Empty queue: g_pStreamQueueHead is NULL, function skips directly to cleanup
  - No valid transfer: Complex multi-condition check at 0x10007C63
  - Alignment: All transfer sizes aligned to 4-byte boundary (& 0xFFFFFFFC)

functions.name: GetSmackSoundBufferSize
functions.comment:
Calculates the current audio buffer size for Smack sound playback.

  Algorithm:
  1. Call FUN_10007c30() for initialization/synchronization
  2. Get current system time via timeGetTime()
  3. Calculate elapsed time: (currentTime - lastUpdateTime)
  4. Scale the sample rate by elapsed time: (sampleRate * elapsed) / 1000
  5. Cap the result to maxBufferSize: min(scaledSize, maxBufferSize)
  6. Return: baseOffset + cappedSize

  Parameters:
  pSoundState (Stack[0x4]:4): Pointer to audio state structure
    Offset 0x14: Sample rate (samples per second, DWORD)
    Offset 0x7c: Last update timestamp (DWORD)
    Offset 0x78: Maximum buffer size (DWORD)
    Offset 0x60: Base buffer offset (DWORD)

  Returns:
  EAX: Current audio buffer size (baseOffset + scaledSamples)

functions.name: ConfigureSmackAudioSample
functions.comment:
Configures a Miles Sound System (MSS) audio sample for Smack video playback.

  Algorithm:
    1. Initialize the AIL sample handle from Smack structure offset 0x40
    2. Compute sample type based on stereo (offset 0x50) and 16-bit (offset 0x54) flags:
       - Stereo + 8-bit:  type = 3
       - Stereo + 16-bit: type = 1
       - Mono + 8-bit:    type = 2
       - Mono + 16-bit:   type = 0
    3. Set sample type and stereo flag via AIL_set_sample_type
    4. Set playback rate from offset 0x48
    5. Associate Smack pointer with sample via AIL_set_sample_user_data
    6. Set initial volume to 0x7f (127, ~50% max)

  Parameters:
    pSmack - Pointer to Smack structure containing audio configuration

  Returns:
    void

  Special Cases:
    - Requires MSS/AIL function pointers to be initialized via SmackSoundUseMSS
    - Sample handle at offset 0x40 must be valid (allocated via AIL_allocate_sample_handle)
    - Volume 0x7f (127) is default; max is 0xff (255)

functions.name: InitializeGameObject
functions.comment:
Initializes a game object structure by zeroing specific fields and calling setup routines.

Algorithm:
  1. Load function pointer from g_pfnObjectInitCallback and call it with value at nObject+0x40
  2. Clear EAX register to 0x00000000
  3. Zero the field at offset 0x60 using cleared EAX value
  4. Zero the field at offset 0x78 using cleared EAX value
  5. Zero the field at offset 0x7c using cleared EAX value
  6. Call FUN_10007ec0(nObject) to perform additional initialization setup
  7. Return control to caller

Parameters:
  nObject - Handle/pointer to object structure to initialize (int type, passed via ESP+0x8)

Returns:
  void - No value returned (EDX:EAX not used for return)

Special Cases:
  - The object must have valid callback handler at offset 0x40
  - Function pointers at g_pfnObjectInitCallback must be properly initialized
  - Three consecutive 4-byte fields are zeroed in sequence (0x60, 0x78, 0x7c)

functions.name: UnlinkListNode
functions.comment:
Unlinks a node from a doubly-linked list structure

Algorithm:
  1. Check if list is initialized (g_pListHead != 0)
  2. Call cleanup callbacks for node fields at offsets 0x40, 0x68, 0x64
  3. If node is list head, update head pointer to next node
  4. Otherwise, traverse list from head until target node found
  5. Update previous node's next pointer to skip target node

Parameters:
  pNode - Pointer to node structure to unlink (passed in ESI)
    Offset 0x3c: Next pointer in list
    Offset 0x40: Field requiring cleanup callback
    Offset 0x64: Field requiring cleanup callback
    Offset 0x68: Field requiring cleanup callback

Returns:
  void (no return value)

Special Cases:
  - Does nothing if list not initialized (g_pListHead == 0)
  - Handles unlinking head node by updating global head pointer
  - Safely handles node not found (traversal stops at NULL)

functions.name: SetSmackSampleVolumePan
functions.comment:
Sets the volume and pan for an MSS (Miles Sound System) audio sample.

  Algorithm:
    1. Clamp dwVolume to maximum 0x8000 (32768)
    2. Convert volume from Smacker range (0-0x8000) to AIL range (0-127):
       - Formula: ((dwVolume * 0x4f6) / 0x8000 + 5) / 10
       - 0x4f6 (1270) chosen so max input yields 127
    3. Call AIL_set_sample_volume with sample handle from Smack+0x40
    4. Convert pan from Smacker range (0-0x10000) to AIL range (0-127):
       - Formula: ((dwPan * 0x4f6) / 0x10000 + 5) / 10
    5. Call AIL_set_sample_pan with same sample handle

  Parameters:
    pSmack   - Pointer to Smack structure; sample handle at offset 0x40
    dwVolume - Volume level (0-0x8000, clamped if exceeds max)
    dwPan    - Pan position (0-0x10000; 0=left, 0x8000=center, 0x10000=right)

  Returns:
    void

  Special Cases:
    - Requires MSS library loaded via SmackSoundUseMSS
    - g_pfnAIL_set_sample_volume and g_pfnAIL_set_sample_pan must be initialized
    - Volume >0x8000 is silently clamped to 0x8000

  Structure Layout (Smack audio-related fields):
    Offset | Size | Field              | Type   | Description
    0x40   | 4    | hAILSample         | HSAMPLE| AIL sample handle for MSS playback

functions.name: _SmackSoundUseDW@12
functions.signature: uint _SmackSoundUseDW@12(uint dwSoundRate, uint dwSoundBits, uint dwSoundChannels)
functions.comment:
Initializes DiamondWare Sound System (DWS) for Smack video audio playback.

Algorithm:
1. Check if sound handler already initialized (g_pfnSmackSoundHandler != NULL)
2. Call GetVersion() to detect Windows version
3. Load DWSW32S.DLL (Win32s) or DWSW32.DLL (Win95/NT) via LoadLibraryA
4. Validate module handle (must be >= 0x20, else fail)
5. Resolve 11 DWS function pointers via GetProcAddress:
   - dws_ErrNo, dws_DGetInfo, dws_DPlay, dws_DDiscard
   - dws_DPause, dws_DUnPause, dws_XDig, dws_DetectHardWare
   - dws_Init, dws_Kill, dws_DClear
6. Validate all function pointers resolved (non-NULL)
7. Store sound parameters in globals
8. Calculate buffer size: (dwSoundBits >> 3) * dwSoundChannels * dwSoundRate
9. Set up Smack sound handler function pointers

Parameters:
  dwSoundRate - Audio sample rate in Hz (e.g., 22050, 44100)
  dwSoundBits - Bits per sample (8 or 16)
  dwSoundChannels - Number of audio channels (1=mono, 2=stereo)

Returns:
  1 (TRUE) - DWS initialized successfully, all function pointers resolved
  0 (FALSE) - Initialization failed:
    - Already initialized
    - LoadLibraryA failed (handle < 0x20)
    - GetProcAddress failed for any DWS function

Global Variables Modified:
  g_hDwsModule - DWS DLL module handle
  g_pfnDwsErrNo, g_pfnDwsDGetInfo, etc. - DWS function pointers
  g_dwSoundRate, g_dwSoundBits, g_dwSoundChannels - Sound configuration
  g_dwSoundBufferSize - Calculated buffer size in bytes
  g_pfnSmackSoundHandler - Main sound handler callback
  g_pfnSmackSoundInit/Open/Close/Mix - Smack sound interface functions

functions.name: InitializeLinkedListNode
functions.comment:
Initializes a linked list node with allocated memory buffers.

Algorithm:
1. Call initialization callback (g_pfnInitializeCallback) with local data
2. If callback fails or returns 0xcb, return error code
3. Calculate scaled value: (wInputValue * field_0x14) / g_dwDivisor
4. Allocate 0x30 bytes (48 bytes) for primary buffer
5. Clear allocated buffer using REP STOSD
6. Allocate additional memory based on scaled value + 0x38
7. Verify secondary allocation succeeded, return error if NULL
8. Store configuration data and set magic value 0x81000000
9. Calculate final scaled value: (g_dwMultiplier * 0x100) / field_0x48
10. Insert node into linked list via g_pLinkedListHead
11. Return success status with upper bytes of scaled value

Parameters:
  ESI  pNode - Pointer to structure (accessed with offsets 0x14, 0x44, 0x60, 0x68, 0x3c, 0x48)

Returns:
  EAX = 0x01 on success with scaled value in upper bytes
  EAX = error code (bottom 24 bits only) on allocation failure or callback error

Special Cases:
  - Callback may return 0x00 or 0xcb as valid results
  - Allocation failures at offset 0x60 or offset 0x4 return error
  - Linked list insertion uses global pointer chain

functions.name: RemoveSmackBuffer
functions.comment:
Removes a SmackBuffer from the global linked list and frees its resources.

Algorithm:
  1. Check if global list head (g_pSmackBufferListHead) is non-NULL
  2. Call cleanup callback function at offset 0x60+0xe for buffer resources
  3. Free internal buffer data allocation at offset 0x60+0x4 using radfree()
  4. Free buffer structure itself (offset 0x60) using radfree()
  5. If buffer is head of list, update head to buffer.next (offset 0x3c)
  6. Otherwise find predecessor by traversing linked list at offset 0x3c
  7. If predecessor found, unlink by setting predecessor.next to buffer.next

Parameters:
  nBuffer: Address of SmackBuffer structure to remove from list

Returns:
  void: Always returns without error status

Special Cases:
  Returns without action if buffer is not in the list
  Returns without action if list head becomes NULL after removal

functions.name: GetInterpolatedValue
functions.comment:
Calculates interpolated animation value based on elapsed time.

Algorithm:
  1. Retrieve current animation state pointer from pAnimation
  2. Get current system time via timeGetTime()
  3. Calculate elapsed time since animation start
  4. If elapsed time < duration: interpolate based on progress ratio
     Interpolated = (MaxValue * ElapsedTime) / Duration
  5. If elapsed time >= duration: return maximum value
  6. Add base value offset to interpolated result

Parameters:
  pAnimation - Pointer to animation structure containing timing and value fields
    Offset 0x6c: Base value (initial offset)
    Offset 0x70: Start time (from timeGetTime())
    Offset 0x74: Duration in milliseconds
    Offset 0x78: Maximum value

Returns:
  int - Interpolated value between base value and (base value + max value)

functions.name: ProcessSmackBufferList
functions.comment:
Processes the Smack buffer list by copying audio data, initializing audio buffers, and updating timing information.

Algorithm:
  1. Iterate through linked list of Smack buffers starting at g_pSmackBufferListHead
  2. For each buffer, check if data is ready to copy (offset 0x10 <= size at offset 0x44 or at offset 0x68)
  3. Initialize audio state (0x8000000) via callback
  4. Copy audio data using MemoryCopyRegions, adjust data size
  5. If not mono (offset 0x50 == 0), XOR each byte with 0x80 (audio data inversion)
  6. Set up audio format structure: sample rate, channels, bit depth
  7. Call audio processing callback for prepared buffer
  8. Update timing: record start time (timeGetTime) or accumulate samples if already running
  9. Move to next buffer in linked list (offset 0x3c)

Parameters:
  None

Returns:
  void - modifies global buffer list in place

Special Cases:
  - Empty buffer list (g_pSmackBufferListHead == NULL): immediate return
  - Mono audio (offset 0x50 != 0): skip XOR inversion loop
  - First buffer in timing sequence: initialize start time
  - Timing overflow: reset timer, accumulate samples

Globals Used:
  g_pSmackBufferListHead - pointer to head of Smack buffer linked list
  g_pfnInitializeCallback - audio init callback (offset 0x10015d34)
  g_pfnProcessSmackStream - stream processor callback (offset 0x10015d54)
  timeGetTime - Windows timer function
  MemoryCopyRegions - buffer copy function

functions.name: ResetSmackSoundStream
functions.comment:
Resets a Smack sound stream by discarding its sound buffer and clearing state fields.

Algorithm:
  1. Get sound buffer pointer from pSmackSound+0x60
  2. Read buffer parameter (word) from buffer+0x0E
  3. Call g_pfnSmackBufferCleanup (dws_DDiscard) with buffer parameter
  4. Clear four DWORD fields at offsets 0x6C, 0x70, 0x74, 0x78 in pSmackSound

Parameters:
  pSmackSound - Pointer to Smack sound structure (passed via stack, __stdcall)

Returns:
  void

Structure Layout (SmackSound offsets accessed):
  Offset | Size | Field         | Description
  0x60   | 4    | pSoundBuffer  | Pointer to sound buffer structure
  0x6C   | 4    | dwField6C     | Cleared to 0 on reset
  0x70   | 4    | dwField70     | Cleared to 0 on reset
  0x74   | 4    | dwField74     | Cleared to 0 on reset
  0x78   | 4    | dwField78     | Cleared to 0 on reset

Note: Function body is malformed in Ghidra (only PUSH ESI visible).
      Full assembly: PUSH ESI; XOR ECX,ECX; MOV ESI,[ESP+8]; MOV EAX,[ESI+0x60];
      MOV CX,[EAX+0x0E]; PUSH ECX; CALL [g_pfnSmackBufferCleanup];
      XOR EAX,EAX; MOV [ESI+0x78],EAX; MOV [ESI+0x74],EAX;
      MOV [ESI+0x70],EAX; MOV [ESI+0x6C],EAX; POP ESI; RET 4

functions.name: ApplyColorScale
functions.signature: void ApplyColorScale(void * pCallback, uint dwColor, uint dwScale)
functions.comment:
Scales color value using 16-bit fixed-point blending arithmetic.

Algorithm:
  1. Clamp input color value to 0xFFFF maximum
  2. If dwScale < 0x8000: apply downscaling (color * scale / 0x8000)
  3. If dwScale > 0x8000: apply upscaling using complement (0x10000 - scale)
  4. Right-shift both color components by 8 bits to extract 16-bit values
  5. Invoke g_pfnColorBlend callback with scaled component parameters
  6. Return (stdcall cleanup)

Parameters:
  pCallback (EDX): Function pointer to color blending callback routine
  dwColor (stack): RGB color value, range 0x0000-0xFFFF
  dwScale (stack): 16-bit fixed-point scale (0x8000=neutral, 0x0000=black, 0x10000=white)

Returns:
  void - Result passed through pCallback invocation with two uint color components

functions.name: _SmackSoundUseWin@0
functions.comment:
Initializes Smack audio subsystem to use Windows waveOut API.

Exported as _SmackSoundUseWin@0 for external Smack library integration.
Sets up function pointer table for Windows multimedia audio output.

Algorithm:
1. Check if sound handler already initialized (g_pfnSmackSoundHandler != NULL)
2. If already initialized, return failure (AL=0)
3. Otherwise, populate all sound callback function pointers:
   - g_pfnSmackSoundInit -> ProcessSmackSoundQueue
   - g_pfnSmackSoundHandler -> SmackSoundInitialize  
   - g_pfnSmackSoundOpen -> RemoveSmackSoundNode
   - g_pfnSmackSoundClose -> LAB_10008a30
   - g_pfnSmackSoundMix -> ResetAudioOutput
   - g_pfnCloseWaveOutCallback -> CloseWaveOutDeviceCallback
   - g_pfnSoundOnCallback -> LAB_10008c90
   - g_pfnSmackSoundCallback -> SetWaveOutVolumePan
4. Return success (0x10008c01, AL=1)

Parameters:
  None - This function takes no parameters (__stdcall with 0 bytes cleanup)

Returns:
  uint - On success: 0x10008c01 (low byte AL=1 indicates success)
         On failure: masked handler address with AL=0 (already initialized)

Special Cases:
- Only one sound system can be active at a time (waveOut, DirectSound, or DirectWave)
- Must be called before any Smack video with audio is opened
- Thread-safe check via g_pfnSmackSoundHandler null test

Related Functions:
- _SmackSoundUseDirectSound@4: Alternative using DirectSound
- _SmackSoundUseDW@12: Alternative using DirectWave
- InitializeMssSoundSystem: MSS/Miles Sound System alternative

functions.name: SmackSoundInitialize
functions.comment:
Initializes a Smack sound buffer for playback

Algorithm:
  1. Calculate required buffer size from input data size (shift >> 2, round to 0x1000)
  2. Allocate memory for sound buffer (calculated_size*2 + 0x40 bytes via radmalloc)
  3. Store allocation pointer in structure at offset +0x64
  4. Calculate and store buffer end pointer at offset +0x68
  5. Store custom parameter (dwParam) at offset +0x78
  6. Call FUN_10008800 to perform internal sound buffer initialization
  7. If init succeeds, link structure to global linked list via g_pSmackSoundListHead
  8. If init fails, free allocated memory and return error code

Parameters:
  pBuffer   Pointer to SmackBuffer structure (passed in ESI, contains sound data info)
  dwParam   Custom parameter value stored at buffer offset +0x78 (purpose varies by caller)

Returns:
  1 (0x00000001)  - Success: Buffer initialized and linked to list
  0 (0x00000000)  - Failure: Either radmalloc failed or FUN_10008800 initialization failed

Special Cases:
  - If radmalloc returns NULL, function exits immediately with return 0
  - If FUN_10008800 returns 0 (failure), previously allocated memory is freed before returning 0
  - Successful init links structure to global list at g_pSmackSoundListHead

Structure Offsets Accessed:
  Offset | Size | Field             | Type     | Description
  0x14   | 4    | dwInputDataSize   | DWORD    | Input data size used to calculate buffer
  0x44   | 4    | dwCalculatedSize  | DWORD    | Calculated buffer size (rounded to 4KB)
  0x64   | 4    | pAllocatedMem     | void*    | Pointer to radmalloc'ed memory
  0x68   | 4    | pBufferEnd        | void*    | Buffer end pointer (alloc + size*2 + 0x20)
  0x78   | 4    | dwCustomParam     | DWORD    | Custom parameter (dwParam)
  0x3c   | 4    | pNextInList       | void*    | Next buffer in linked list

functions.name: OpenWaveOutDevice
functions.comment:
Initialize waveOut audio device and prepare audio output buffers for playback

Algorithm:
  1. Build WAVEFORMATEX structure from audio context: sample rate (0x48), 
     channels (0x54), bits per sample (0x50)
  2. Check g_bDebugAudio flag and log "Using standard waveOut" if enabled
  3. Call waveOutOpen with WAVE_MAPPER device (-1), format struct, and context callback
  4. On success: initialize two audio buffers at offsets 0x64, 0x68
  5. Clear buffer headers (32 bytes each) with memset
  6. Prepare both wave headers via waveOutPrepareHeader
  7. Generate silence pattern: 0x80 for 8-bit audio, 0x00 for 16-bit audio
  8. Fill first buffer with silence using efficient DWORD writes
  9. Call waveOutWrite to start playback
  10. Poll timeGetTime with 1000ms timeout for WHDR_DONE flag on buffer
  11. Return success (1) if playback completes, or call FUN_100089d0 if timeout

Parameters:
  nAudioContext [ESP+0x04]  - Address of audio context structure
                              Offset 0x40: HWAVEOUT device handle storage
                              Offset 0x44: DWORD buffer size in bytes  
                              Offset 0x48: DWORD sample rate (Hz)
                              Offset 0x50: DWORD bits per sample (0=16-bit, other=8-bit)
                              Offset 0x54: DWORD channel count minus 1
                              Offset 0x64: LPWAVEHDR pointer to first buffer
                              Offset 0x68: LPWAVEHDR pointer to second buffer
                              Offset 0x78: DWORD callback flags

Returns:
  EAX = 0x00000001  - Playback succeeded and completed within timeout
  EAX = 0x00000000  - Playback completed (normal path)
  EAX = MMRESULT    - waveOutOpen failed with specific MMSYSERR error code
  
Special Cases:
  - No output device: waveOutOpen returns MMSYSERR_NODEVICE
  - Device busy: waveOutOpen returns MMSYSERR_ALLOCATED
  - Timeout occurs: Marks buffer with WHDR_DONE and calls cleanup function
  - 8-bit audio: Uses 0x80 fill pattern, 16-bit uses 0x00 (silence)

functions.name: CloseWaveOutDevice
functions.comment:
Closes and cleans up the wave output device.

Algorithm:
  1. Check if wave output handle exists at offset 0x40
  2. Call waveOutReset to reset the wave output device
  3. Spin-wait for first wave header (offset 0x64) dwFlags & 1 to be set
  4. Spin-wait for second wave header (offset 0x68) dwFlags & 1 to be set
  5. Call waveOutUnprepareHeader for first buffer (offset 0x64)
  6. Call waveOutUnprepareHeader for second buffer (offset 0x68)
  7. Call waveOutClose to close wave output device
  8. Set wave output handle to NULL

Parameters:
  nAudioContext: Base address of audio context structure containing wave state

Returns:
  void - No return value

Special Cases:
  If wave output handle is NULL, function returns immediately without cleanup

functions.name: ProcessSmackSoundQueue
functions.comment:
Processes Smack sound playback queue by writing audio data to wave device.

  Algorithm:
  1. Iterate through linked list of Smack sound structures (g_pSmackSoundListHead)
  2. For each sound, check if both input wave headers (0x64, 0x68) are ready (flag 0x1)
  3. Validate buffer size > 3 bytes and select ready wave header
  4. Copy audio data from sound buffer to wave header using MemoryCopyRegions
  5. Update residual buffer size and clear ready flag from wave header (AND 0xfffffffe)
  6. Fill remaining buffer space with silence bytes (0x80 for mono, duplicated for DWORD fills)
  7. Submit filled wave header to waveOutWrite with size 0x20 (32)
  8. Update timing counters: store current timestamp if first write, else track elapsed time
  9. Calculate playback time in milliseconds: (dwBufferLength * 1000) / nSampleRate
  10. Move to next sound in linked list via offset 0x3c

  Parameters:
  (none)

  Returns:
  (none)

  Special Cases:
  - Silence fill pattern: 0x80808080 for stereo/multi-byte, 0x80 for remaining bytes
  - Mono vs stereo determined by field at offset 0x50 (0 = mono, 1 = stereo)
  - Timing only updated if buffer successfully written
  - Loop continues until linked list tail reached (puVar6 == NULL)
